doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Impulse Sun Ra recordings and Ed Michel
summary: Prompted by Goodwillie, Gordon recalls Ed Michel's role with Impulse and Blue Thumb Sun Ra releases and a quadraphonic master.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: How did you manage to get the Impulse recordings? Did you work with Creed Taylor in the unreleased Impulse sessions?
No. It’s not like that Christian. The — let’s see, who was the producer that worked for Impulse and other companies?
Not Bob Thiele. Who produced “Space is the Place”? I’m forgetting his name right now.
Excuse me, I’m going to look it up on the computer unless you want to.
Yeah, I’m actually doing it right now.
Yes. The album. Blue Thumb, 1973, technical, Ed Michel?

And he passed away not that long ago, a major, major important factor in jazz, I don’t know how often he’s been interviewed, I don’t really know what’s been written about him, but he is one of the heroes of jazz and record labels. He — I’m sure he was the one who encouraged Impulse, a division of ABC at that point, not an Indy anymore, to license Sun Ra recordings and make new Sun Ra recordings. And it wasn’t just Sun Ra, very important jazz figure. And by the way, Impulse for a while dallied with quadraphonic recordings, and that was really interesting, where you’d see like these — behind the store, these quadraphonic Sun Ra recordings and you’d go, “What?” I need a quadraphonic record player, you know, to properly, you know, I don’t even know if they ever sold a single one or what it was or what the decoding — who knew what that was. I had no idea. But interestingly enough we had gotten from Alton a quadraphonic tape. Here’s one of your masters. It’s in quadraphonic. And so Roger Seibel had to mix down this quadraphonic, you know, recording to you know a regular recording, you know, coming out of two speakers or whatever. That was a whole trip. But the — I forget Christian, why I went off on this tangent. But yeah, they started doing — Ed Michel helped to institute some kind of program I believe to issue these records on Impulse, and then a masterpiece on Blue Thumb, “Space is the Place” which I think was a quadraphonic recording also.
